faq.q: Does this translator send my text to a server?
faq.a: Yes, unlike the other tools on the site. Translation needs a model too large for a browser, so it calls the MyMemory translation API, meaning your text does leave your device. The page states this plainly and advises against pasting confidential material. Your recent translations are also kept locally (last 10) under translator_history for quick reuse.

faq.q: Which languages and the auto-detect are supported?
faq.a: The dropdowns list over 20 languages including English, Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Punjabi, Odia, Assamese, Urdu, Spanish, French, German, Arabic, Chinese, Japanese, Russian, Portuguese, Korean, and Italian. Source can be set to Auto Detect, which is sent to the API as 'Autodetect'; when used it reports back the detected language name.

faq.q: How does it handle long text?
faq.a: Input is split into 500-character chunks that are translated one after another, with a progress bar and a 'Translating chunk X/Y' status. If the service returns a rate-limit (429) it tells you to wait and retry, and failed requests are retried automatically after a short pause. There's also a soft warning once your input passes 5000 characters.

faq.q: Can I hear the translation or save it?
faq.a: Yes. The 'Speak' button uses your browser's speech synthesis, trying to match a voice to the target language (availability depends on your device). You can also Copy the result or download it as translation.txt. Typing pauses for about 0.8 seconds auto-triggers a translation, and the swap (⇄) button exchanges the two languages and their text boxes.
